02-026.r: Harappan boat models → Lothal (clay model boats) and Mohenjodaro (seals showing boats).

02-027.r: Not true of Indus civilization: knew iron (it was a Bronze Age culture). True: covered drains, advanced internal and external trade, Mother Goddess worship.

02-028.r: Harappan, not true: same-size bricks everywhere (ornamental bricks at Kalibangan, curved at Chanhudaro); all houses single-storey (some had two). True: main roads about ten metres wide.

02-029.r: Indus Valley Civilization known for town planning, Mohenjodaro and Harappa, agriculture (Kalibangan ploughed field) and industry/trade → all four.

02-030.r: Wrong pair: Kalibangan is in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, not Haryana; found by Luigi Pio Tessitory, excavated by A. Ghosh (1950-52). Alamgirpur-U.P., Lothal-Gujarat, Ropar-Punjab correct.

02-031.r: Harappan sites in U.P. → Alamgirpur (Meerut) and Hulas (Saharanpur); Kalibangan → Rajasthan; Lothal → Gujarat.

02-033.r: Harappan sites in U.P. → Mandi (Muzaffarnagar; hoard of Harappan gold ornaments) and Hulas (Saharanpur; Late Harappan). Rakhigarhi → Hisar, Haryana.

02-034.r: Wrong pair: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar, Haryana (on Ghaggar), not Rajasthan. Correct: Alamgirpur-U.P., Banawali-Haryana, Daimabad-Maharashtra.

02-035.r: Harappan limits: East → Alamgirpur (Meerut, U.P.); West → Sutkagendor (Baluchistan); North → Manda (J&K); South → Daimabad (Maharashtra).
02-035.h: Read the compass N-S-E-W as Manda, Daimabad, Alamgirpur, Sutkagendor.

02-036.r: Manda → Jammu-Kashmir; Daimabad → Maharashtra; Kalibangan → Rajasthan; Rakhigarhi → Haryana.

02-037.r: Balu → Haryana; Manda → Jammu and Kashmir; Padri → Gujarat; Hulas → Uttar Pradesh.

02-038.r: Harappan sites in Sindh (Pakistan) → Mohenjodaro and Chanhudaro; Harappa → Punjab (Pakistan); Surkotada → Gujarat.

02-040.r: Chanhudaro (about 130 km south of Mohenjodaro) → found by N.G. Majumdar (1931); excavated by E.J.H. Mackay (1935-36); bead-making factory and furnace.

02-041.r: Harappa (on Ravi; Sahiwal district, Punjab) → now in Pakistan. In India: Kalibangan (Rajasthan), Lothal (Gujarat), Alamgirpur (U.P.).

02-042.r: Rangpur (Harappan-contemporary site) → Saurashtra, Gujarat; people grew rice, bajra and sorghum.

02-043.r: Dadheri (Kotla Dadheri, Fatehgarh Sahib) → late Harappan site in Punjab; known for Painted Grey Ware.

02-044.r: Lothal → Indus site in India: Ahmedabad district, Gujarat, on Bhogava river; discovered by S.R. Rao in 1954. Harappa and Mohenjodaro are in Pakistan.

02-047.r: Port city of the Indus Valley Civilization → Lothal (only Indus site with evidence of a port).

02-049.r: Indus city trading with West Asia → Lothal (Gujarat), harbour on the Gulf of Khambhat.

02-050.r: Main Indus features: burnt-brick buildings (Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro; drains at Lothal), planned architecture, advanced trade → answer 'more than one of the above'.

02-051.r: Terracotta plough model (Harappan) → Banawali (Fatehabad, Haryana), also Cholistan. Kalibangan (Rajasthan) → ploughed field of the early phase, not a plough model.
02-051.c: Terracotta plough models come from Banawali (and Cholistan); Kalibangan gave a ploughed field, not a plough model. So (d) Banawali is the answer; the book wrongly counts Kalibangan too.

02-053.r: Pataliputra (near Patna) → not an Indus site. Indus sites: Kalibangan, Ropar, Lothal.

02-054.r: Largest Harappan site in India → Rakhigarhi (Hisar district, Haryana).

02-056.r: Indus civilization rivers → Sindhu, Chenab, Jhelum (also Ravi, Sutlej); spread from Jhelum to Hindon (Yamuna tributary, Alamgirpur); not the Ganga.

02-057.r: Indus beliefs (probable): Mother Goddess and Shiva worship; fire pits suggest Yagya; burials show belief in spirit (atma); human sacrifice evidence at Mohenjodaro.
02-057.c: No single answer: the explanation supports Mother Goddess worship, rituals and sacrifice (fire pits, human sacrifice) and belief in spirit, so several options fit.

02-058.r: Indus people worshipped Shiva (Pashupati): Marshall's Pashupati seal shows a three-faced god in yogic posture with rhino, buffalo, elephant and tiger.

02-059.r: Harappa and Mohenjodaro found under ASI Director-General Sir John Marshall (1902-1928): Dayaram Sahni → Harappa (1921); Rakhal Das Banerjee → Mohenjodaro.

02-061.r: Wrong pair: Dholavira was excavated by R.S. Bisht, not B.K. Thapar. Correct: Harappa-Daya Ram Sahni; Lothal-S.R. Rao; Surkotada-J.P. Joshi.

02-062.r: First to dig at Harappa but missed its significance → Alexander Cunningham (visits 1853 and 1856; found pottery, tools and a stone seal).

02-063.r: Not linked with Harappa/Mohenjodaro excavation → V.A. Smith. Linked: Daya Ram Sahni (Harappa, 1921), M.S. Vats, R.D. Banerjee (Mohenjodaro, 1922), K.N. Dikshit, Mackay.

02-064.r: Surkotada (Kachchh, Gujarat) → discovered and excavated by Jagatpati Joshi.

02-065.r: Wells and bathrooms in houses (mature Harappan) → found in almost every major Indus city.
02-065.c: Mohenjodaro is the site best known for wells in houses, so (d) is the likeliest intended answer; the book prints none because wells occur at most major Indus cities.

02-066.r: Order of appearance: urban culture (Harappan) → iron plough (around 1000 B.C.) → punch-marked silver coins (7th-6th century B.C.) → gold coins (Indo-Greeks).

02-067.r: First metal used by man → copper.

02-069.r: Metal not found at Harappan sites → iron. Found: gold, silver, copper, brass (Bronze Age). Iron Age in India from later Vedic period (about 1000 B.C.).

02-070.r: Banawali (Fatehabad, Haryana) → Harappan site in the valley of Ghaggar and its tributaries.

02-071.r: True: Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Ropar, Kalibangan are main Indus sites; Harappans built roads, housing and covered drains. False: they did not know metals.

02-072.r: Mohenjodaro (Larkana, Sindh) and Harappa (Sahiwal, Punjab, Pakistan) are dead cities; both found by excavation → A and R true, R not the explanation.

02-073.r: Rock-cut architecture (Harappan) → Dholavira (Rann of Kachchh, Gujarat): second largest Indian Harappan site after Rakhigarhi; excavated by R.S. Bisht (1992); rock-cut reservoir.

02-075.r: Harappan city in three parts (Citadel, Middle town, Lower town) → Dholavira, Kachchh, Gujarat.
02-075.h: Dholavira = three-tier town: Citadel, Middle, Lower.

02-077.r: Water harvesting with a series of dams and connected reservoirs → Dholavira (Gujarat).

02-078.r: Advanced Harappan water management → Dholavira: rock-cut reservoir about 79 m × 12 m, 7 m deep; water stored by building dams.

02-079.r: Double burials (Harappan) → Lothal (three found) and Kalibangan; also Rakhigarhi.
02-079.c: Lothal is the site usually given for double burials (the book counts three there); the book prints no answer because it also cites Kalibangan.

02-080.r: Sinauli/Sonauli (Baraut, Baghpat, U.P.) → 125 Harappan graves, north-south oriented, mostly primary human burials.

02-081.r: Mandi (Muzaffarnagar, U.P.) → late Harappan jewellery hoard dug up by villagers, June 2000.

02-082.r: Cotton for clothing first grown in India (about 3000 B.C.; Egypt 2500 B.C.); the Greeks called it 'Sindon'.
02-082.h: Sindon from Sindhu: cotton went from the Indus to Greece.

02-083.r: Indus people worshipped both male and female deities (true). No palaces or temples found; no horse-drawn war chariots → only statement 2 correct.

02-084.r: Indus civilization → largely secular (no theocracy or organised religion); cotton used for textiles. Both statements correct.

02-085.r: Famous humped bull seal → Mohenjodaro (Sindh; excavated by R.D. Banerjee, 1922).

02-086.r: 'Dancing Girl' of Mohenjo-daro → bronze, cast by the lost-wax technique; about 10.5 cm high.

02-087.r: Tree shown often on Indus seals → Pipal (sacred); seals mostly of steatite and square.

02-088.r: Animal not on Harappan seals → horse. Seals show one-horned animal (most common), buffalo, tiger, rhinoceros, goat, elephant.
02-088.t: Horse: known but absent from seals. Lion: no remains found at all.

02-089.r: Animal whose remains are not found in Indus Civilization → lion. Cow and elephant found; horse disputed, but latest excavation shows evidence.

02-090.r: Animal taken as unknown to Indus people → horse (BPSC key); bull (Zebu seal) and elephant known. Horse disputed and played no major role.
02-090.c: Explanation says the latest excavation shows horse evidence; answer follows the BPSC key.

02-091.r: IIT Kharagpur study → 900 years of continuous low rainfall (drought) caused the fall of the Indus Valley Civilisation.

02-092.r: Terracotta cake with horned deity (other side: goat dragged by a man) → Kalibangan; also a series of fire altars on mud-brick platforms.

02-093.r: Egyptian Civilization → banks of the Nile ('lifeline of Egypt') for almost 3,000 years. Indus and Mesopotamia were contemporary civilizations.
